title: Security on-call: evidence handoff & SIEM export playbook
body:
Purpose
This playbook defines the on-call security team's procedures for capturing, validating, and handing off digital evidence during incidents that require SIEM export or deeper forensic analysis. It ties together RBAC v2 responsibilities, the audit log schema, automated evidence export pipelines, and the post-incident handoff process.

Audience
Primary: on-call security engineers, incident responders, SREs called into security incidents.
Secondary: audit/compliance reviewers, legal, engineering managers.

High-level goals
- Ensure evidence is captured consistently and immutably (hash, origin, retention policy).
- Maintain clear RBAC responsibilities for who can request/approve evidence exports.
- Provide reproducible SIEM queries and export steps to avoid data loss or sprawl.
- Produce a minimal, consistent postmortem evidence bundle for auditors and legal.

When to use this playbook
- Confirmed compromise, data exfiltration suspicion, suspicious privilege escalation, or any request from legal/IR that demands definitive audit data.
- When SIEM event ranges need to be frozen and exported for legal hold.

Pre-incident setup (checks that must be green before going on-call)
- RBAC v2: ensure on-call role (sec:oncall) has the following temporary privileges: SIEM read, audit-log:export-request, evidence:snapshot-initiate. Permanent roles should not have export permissions; use just-in-time elevation via SSO/Okta approver.
- Audit log schema verified against latest spec: required fields present = [event_id, ts_iso, principal_id, principal_role, action, resource_type, resource_id, req_id, src_ip, user_agent, outcome, request_payload_sha256, response_payload_sha256, shard_id].
- Evidence export pipeline (terraform-managed) tested weekly: test export creates snapshot S3 prefix under s3://redwood-evidence/test/ and sets retention & encryption.
- KMS keys listed: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345. Confirm key access, rotation status.
- SIEM indices mapping: prod-audit-logs -> index:audit-prod-YYYYMM, app-telemetry -> index:app-prod-YYYYMM, network-flow -> index:netflow-prod-YYYYMM.

Immediate steps when an incident is declared
1) Triage and scope (first 10–15 minutes)
   - Record incident ID: use IR-YYYYMMDD-XXX.
   - Confirm on-call role and request JIT elevation if needed. Note approver in incident channel.
   - Short description (1–2 lines) and suspected time range.
   - Start a dedicated Slack channel: #ir-IR-YYYYMMDD-XXX (use template).

2) Preserve volatile evidence (first 30 minutes)
   - If hosts are involved, do not reboot. Collect volatile memory snapshots only when approved by lead. Use host-agent: /opt/infra/bin/collect-memory --host host-id --out s3://redwood-evidence/IR-YYYYMMDD-XXX/memory/host-id.mem.gpg.
   - For containers, capture container logs via: kubectl logs <pod> --since-time=<ISO> > /tmp/pod-logs && upload using evidence-ingest tool.
   - Take live snapshots of audit-log segments: run SIEM range export (see SIEM export queries below) and write to evidence prefix.

3) SIEM export (recommended tool: elasticsearch snapshot or Splunk export)
   - Use approved export tool (evidence-export-cli) which enforces retention and KMS encryption. Example command: evidence-export-cli --index "audit-prod-*" --start "2024-09-02T12:00:00Z" --end "2024-09-02T13:30:00Z" --query "principal_id: \"user:svc-account\" AND outcome:FAILURE" --out s3://redwood-evidence/IR-YYYYMMDD-XXX/siem/audit-export.ndjson.gpg --kms-key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345 --tag IR-YYYYMMDD-XXX
   - Do not run wide open exports without approval. If range > 24 hours, justify to SOC lead and record in incident doc.

4) Audit log schema validation (automated check + manual spot check)
   - Run audit-schema-validator against exported file: audit-schema-validator --file audit-export.ndjson.gpg --schema v2. Expected output: PASS, row-count, missing-fields list (should be empty).
   - Manual sanity checks: verify event_id uniqueness for the range, check presence of request_payload_sha256 for actions that mutate resources, confirm src_ip format, and ensure timestamps are monotonic.

5) Evidence integrity & cataloging
   - Compute and store SHA256 of each artifact: sha256sum file -> store in manifest.json at s3://redwood-evidence/IR-YYYYMMDD-XXX/manifest. Manifest fields: artifact_path, sha256, created_by, created_ts, kms_key, retention_ttl_days. (This repo is generated by evidence-ingest tool automatically.)
   - Tag all objects with tag: ir_id=IR-YYYYMMDD-XXX, case_owner=<person>.

6) RBAC approvals and audit trail
   - Any export > 1GB requires 2 approvers: SOC lead and Legal on-call. Use Okta approval flow and record approver UIDs in the incident doc.
   - Record ticket keys of approval in the incident channel and incident page.

7) Hand-off to forensic team / legal / auditors
   - Compose minimal evidence bundle: manifest.json, audit-export.ndjson.gpg, host memory snapshots (if any), container logs, and a short README.txt describing how exports were generated and verified.
   - Upload bundle to secure evidence bucket path: s3://redwood-evidence/handoffs/IR-YYYYMMDD-XXX/<team>/ and send secure link to receiving party.
   - Create a delivery record in case management system (JIRA-SEC-<id>) with the link and approver list.

8) Post-incident: evidence retention and deletion policy
   - Default retention for IR evidence: 365 days unless legal hold exists. Evidence objects must carry retention_ttl_days metadata and lifecycle rules to expire.
   - If legal hold requested, escalate to compliance with case_id and set indefinite retention. Document legal hold ticket.

SIEM queries (examples)
- Audit failures for a principal: principal_id:"user:alice@redwood.com" AND outcome:FAILURE AND ts_iso:["2024-09-02T00:00:00Z" TO "2024-09-02T23:59:59Z"]
- Privilege escalation (example heuristics): action:("role.grant" OR "role.modify") AND principal_role:!="admin" AND ts_iso:>="2024-09-01T00:00:00Z"
- Large data movement: action:("s3.put_object" OR "object.copy") AND bytes:[1000000000 TO *]
- Abnormal new principal creation: action:"principal.create" AND NOT principal_id.keyword:/(service-|bot-)/

Audit log schema quick reference (required fields)
- event_id (string)
- ts_iso (ISO8601 timestamp)
- principal_id (string) -> canonical: user:<email> or svc:<name>
- principal_role (string)
- action (string)
- resource_type (string)
- resource_id (string)
- req_id (request-id header)
- src_ip (ip string)
- user_agent (string)
- outcome (SUCCESS|FAILURE|UNKNOWN)
- request_payload_sha256 (hex)
- response_payload_sha256 (hex)
- shard_id (string) -> for routing debug

Notes on RBAC v2 responsibilities during IR
- sec:oncall (temporary role): can request exports and kick off evidence pipeline but cannot delete artifacts.
- sec:lead: can approve exports > 1GB and change retention for incident artifacts.
- legal:oncall: required approver for exports involving user PIIs or long-term retention.
- infra:sre: required for any host or cluster-level forensic snapshot.

Checklist (copy into incident doc)
- [ ] Incident ID created and channel spun up
- [ ] JIT elevation requested and approved
- [ ] SIEM export initiated and path recorded
- [ ] Audit schema validator passed
- [ ] Manifest with SHA256 created
- [ ] Evidence bucket path created and tags applied
- [ ] Approvals recorded (SOC, Legal if needed)
- [ ] Evidence bundle handed off and delivery ticket created

Postmortem minimum contents (attach to the incident ticket)
- Summary of impact and timeline (who, what, when, scope)
- What evidence was collected (paths + hashes)
- SIEM queries used and results summary (row counts, notable events)
- RBAC actions observed and any role misconfigurations found
- Root cause hypothesis and next steps (patches, revocations, alerts)
- Lessons learned and policy changes (retention, schema changes, RBAC tweaks)
- Owner for follow-ups and target dates

Appendix A: Common CLI snippets
- Basic export: evidence-export-cli --index "audit-prod-*" --start "<ISO>" --end "<ISO>" --out s3://redwood-evidence/IR-<id>/siem/export.ndjson.gpg --kms-key <arn> --tag <ir>
- Validate schema: audit-schema-validator --file export.ndjson.gpg --schema v2
- Generate manifest: evidence-ingest --register s3://redwood-evidence/IR-<id> --output manifest.json

Appendix B: Troubleshooting notes (notes to self)
- If evidence-export-cli times out for large ranges, split into daily chunks and run in parallel. Always reassemble and re-validate hashes.
- If audit-schema-validator flags missing request_payload_sha256 for mutation events, check upstream logging sidecar configuration and open JIRA: JIRA-LOG-204.
- If KMS access denied, check KeyPolicy vs IAM principal in account 123456789012; use emergency escalation if needed.

TODOs
- [ ] Add example splunk search equivalents and dashboards for rapid triage (Priya)
- [ ] Add play for retention disputes with legal (Luis)

Open questions
- Should default export size threshold for 2-approver flow be 500MB instead of 1GB? (ops cost vs privacy)
- Do we want a read-only evidence access role for external auditors rather than ad-hoc handoffs?

Contact list (on-call rotation)
- sec:oncall: asha.mehta@redwood.com
- sec:lead: daniel.kim@redwood.com
- legal:oncall: priya.nair@redwood.com
- infra:sre: luis.ortega@redwood.com

Last reviewed: 2024-12-03 by Asha Mehta.

End of playbook
